_meta.epistemics_warning: Observational findings, not ground truth. Re-validate on new checkpoints / ORT versions / EPs before relying on a finding to skip work.

findings.title: The class-like remote model_type is not covered by canonical SegFormer registration
findings.observation: On current main 2b9ec0e9e57bba8003d25eaff85f8c7c9e30d75a, ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet@e2bf8e4460fc8fa32bba5ea4d94b3233d367b0e4 reports model_type SegformerForSemanticSegmentation. Optimum 2.1.0 and WinML 0.3.0 registered image-segmentation only for canonical segformer; explicit task/class config still failed before export. The accepted CPU recipes therefore select image-segmentation, AutoModelForImageSegmentation, the literal model_type, and trust_remote_code.

not_yet_tested_on: other remote-code checkpoints that reuse SegformerForSemanticSegmentation as a literal model_type

gotchas: Do not apply the BiRefNet path to ordinary canonical SegFormer checkpoints from the model_type string alone; discriminate with trusted auto_map and architectures metadata.
findings.mechanism_notes: The planner's registry probe and no-recipe current-main config/build failures isolate the literal model_type registration gap.

findings.title: FP32 and FP16 require distinct export paths and opsets for this checkpoint
findings.observation: Resolved build configs for ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet use static x [1,3,1024,1024] and logits [1,1,1024,1024] with ImageNet-normalized value range [-2.1179039301310043, 2.64]. FP32 uses legacy export (dynamo=false), opset 17, and gelu/highdimRTR_lowdimRTR/matmul_add optimization. FP16 uses torch-dynamo (dynamo=true), opset 18, highdimRTR_lowdimRTR only, and quant.mode=fp16 with fp16_keep_io_types=true.
gotchas: Do not infer that the FP32 legacy/opset-17 recipe can be converted to FP16 by changing only quant.mode; the accepted FP16 tuple changes exporter and opset.
findings.mechanism_notes: The final tester-owned winml_build_config.json files and structural manifests agree on requested and actual exporter/opset/dtype contracts.

findings.title: Dynamo metadata traces substantially more BiRefNet modules than legacy tracing
findings.observation: Final HTP metadata for ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet records 220,176,498 parameters and 665 modules for both tuples. FP32 legacy TracingHierarchyBuilder traced 164/665 modules (24.7%) in 95.324s; FP16 DynamoMetadataTagger traced 501/665 modules (75.3%) in 451.695s. Both expose the SwinTransformer backbone and Decoder hierarchy, but the Dynamo path retains finer module scopes.
gotchas: Trace coverage ratios are exporter-path observations, not architecture coverage guarantees; preserve unmapped graph nodes explicitly.
findings.mechanism_notes: Counts come directly from final export_htp_metadata.json artifacts.

findings.title: The final FP32 CPU artifact is a static opset-17 FLOAT model with co-located external data
findings.observation: WinML 0.3.0 / ORT 1.24.5 built ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet FP32 in 402.250s. The final artifact has x FLOAT [1,3,1024,1024], logits FLOAT [1,1,1024,1024], 736 FLOAT and 218 INT64 initializers, 7,787 nodes, no duplicate producers, no raw DeformConv, 6,957 hierarchy-tagged nodes, and a co-located 1,002,702,592-byte model.onnx.data file.
gotchas: The 48 com.microsoft Gelu nodes are expected on the accepted FP32 path; unexpected custom domains remain zero.
findings.mechanism_notes: Final structural manifest passed ONNX/ORT loading and recursive producer checks.

findings.title: The final FP16 CPU artifact is a true static opset-18 FLOAT16 model
findings.observation: WinML 0.3.0 / ORT 1.24.5 built ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet FP16 in 844.469s with --precision fp16. The final artifact has x/logits FLOAT16 at [1,3,1024,1024]/[1,1,1024,1024], 806 FLOAT16 and 207 INT64 initializers, 12,477 nodes, no duplicate producers, no custom domains or raw DeformConv, 7,506 hierarchy-tagged nodes, and a co-located 503,503,744-byte model.onnx.data file.
gotchas: The FP16 file is about half the FP32 external-data size, but the graph has 4,391 Cast nodes and more total nodes; size reduction does not imply a simpler graph.
findings.mechanism_notes: Final structural manifest and ORT CPU session load confirm realized dtype and opset rather than relying on the recipe filename.

findings.title: CPU FP16 runtime was slower and used more inference RSS than FP32
findings.observation: On the same static 1024 CPU workload, ORT 1.24.5 FP32 mean/p50 latency was 17,388.171/17,497.655ms with 5,921.71MB inference RSS delta; FP16 was 19,865.985/19,925.766ms with 6,357.54MB inference RSS delta. Throughput was 0.06 versus 0.05 samples/s. These are tuple-specific measurements, not a general CPU precision ranking.
gotchas: Do not advertise FP16 as a CPU speed or memory optimization for this checkpoint from artifact size alone.
findings.mechanism_notes: The measurements are confirmed; the exact cause of slower FP16 CPU execution was not isolated. Cast-heavy graph structure is a plausible contributor, not a proven cause.

findings.title: FP32 PyTorch-to-ONNX parity passed on the exact static input
findings.observation: For ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet FP32 on the pinned DIS5K image and static [1,3,1024,1024] tensor, PyTorch versus ORT logits cosine was 0.9999999999991248 with max-abs 0.001285552978515625; sigmoid-mask cosine was 0.9999999999995249 with max-abs 0.00005751848220825195 and binary agreement 1.0. PyTorch inference took 20.283s and ORT inference 17.275s.

validated_on: ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet @ fp32 @ CPUExecutionProvider @ pinned DIS5K row 1

gotchas: This single-input parity result is separate from the FP16 tuple and does not transfer to it.
findings.mechanism_notes: The harness used the same named input tensor for the public PyTorch forward and ORT inference.

findings.title: Exact CPU FP16 PyTorch parity is compute-bound before logits at 1024x1024
findings.observation: For ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet FP16, the offline pinned model/artifact hashes and exact float16 [1,3,1024,1024] input hash were verified; local-only load completed in 1.865s and all parameters/buffers were torch.float16. One inference_mode public forward remained live at last durable phase pt_forward:before. Equivalent-path observations lasted 902.688s, 301.094s, and 1,144.430s (2,348.212s cumulative); the final attempt reached 1,787.672 child CPU-seconds and 1,928,876,032 bytes RSS. No PT logits, parity JSON, cosine, max-abs, or accuracy value was emitted.

validated_on: ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet @ fp16 @ CPU PyTorch 2.13.0 @ exact static 1024 input
not_yet_tested_on: completion of the exact public forward to logits

gotchas: This is neither parity PASS nor artifact FAIL: L0 and L1 independently passed for the exact FP16 artifact.
No smaller-input, shortcut, internal-submodule, or prior-logit evidence exists; do not use one to impute numeric parity.
feature_gaps_filed: FILE: provide a phase-checkpointable or otherwise bounded CPU FP16 PyTorch reference path for large static image models so L2 can reach logits without replacing the public forward or changing the parity input.
findings.mechanism_notes: Flushed phase events, growing CPU time, bounded RSS, and three equivalent-path observations locate the timeout inside the single public PyTorch forward and distinguish live compute from crash or model-load failure.

findings.title: Static Analyze found partial accelerator rules but no unsupported operator types
findings.observation: Standalone rule aggregation classified all 7,787 FP32 nodes across 23 op types and all 12,477 FP16 nodes across 26 op types. FP32 mapped 5,840 nodes; FP16 mapped 7,493. QNN NPU and OpenVINO NPU marked Gather, Pad, and Reshape partial; FP16 additionally marked Erf partial on QNN NPU. No operator type was classified unsupported. FP32 dominant counts include Gather 1,384, Unsqueeze 1,200, Mul 971; FP16 includes Cast 4,391, Gather 1,384, Unsqueeze 1,200.

validated_on: ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet @ fp32/fp16 @ static Analyze rule set 121981b72977d956594953334aa85e3a99592cf4ea3fdb3d3e0898b972bac78e

gotchas: These are static rule classifications, not runtime EP support claims.
Half-resolution and fusion functional regions lacked unique serialized tags; their nodes remain in the explicit unmapped totals rather than being guessed.
findings.mechanism_notes: Aggregate artifacts reconcile mapped plus unmapped nodes to each final graph and retain all 12 EP/device rows.

findings.title: L3 evidence is an FP32-only one-row functional smoke
findings.observation: The final FP32 CPU path processed one hash-pinned nobg/DIS5K DIS_VD row at revision e007e9a3af50dec16d0fca3c0856793d20b9a448, with no crops, tiles, or augmentation. Sigmoid/0.5-threshold output produced binary mIoU 0.9659138986825014 and Dice 0.982661447512863 after resizing to 2592x3872. This proves one end-to-end FP32 functional path only; it is not benchmark accuracy and supplies no FP16 accuracy evidence.

validated_on: ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet @ fp32 @ CPUExecutionProvider @ one pinned DIS5K DIS_VD row

gotchas: Never use the one-row FP32 mIoU/Dice values as an FP16 or benchmark-quality claim.
findings.mechanism_notes: Dataset revision, row selection, preprocessing, threshold, pixel counts, and no-benchmark disclaimer are preserved in the tester verdict.

findings.title: FP16 finalization needed deterministic recursive node naming and explicit precision boundaries
findings.observation: Historical FP16 repair evidence for ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet showed 18 unnamed Max nodes caused repeated ORT-generated _input_cast_0/_output_cast_0 producers, while existing Cast(to=FLOAT) boundaries became type-invalid and a FLOAT zero initializer was intentionally retained for blocked Max consumers. The accepted repair assigns globally unique names across graphs/functions, preserves blocked FLOAT casts, and inserts explicit shared casts for blocked-op consumers; the final graph has zero duplicate producers and all floating initializers stored as FLOAT16.

not_yet_tested_on: other large Dynamo graphs with repeated unnamed blocked nodes
nested local-function consumers on model-scale artifacts

gotchas: Blindly converting every FLOAT initializer breaks blocked-op FLOAT contracts; storage conversion and consumer precision boundaries must be handled together.
findings.mechanism_notes: Repair-r3 unit coverage and the final exact FP16 structure/ORT load confirm the generalized conversion path.

findings.title: Hierarchy metadata must survive exporter, optimizer, and FP16 finalization as one pipeline contract
findings.observation: Historical BiRefNet repair evidence found HTP tags keyed by transient Python protobuf wrapper identity did not serialize, and destructive optimizer stages had no pipeline-level metadata snapshot. The accepted repair assigns stable names before tagging and recursively captures/restores model and node metadata across graphs/functions and generated casts. Final artifacts retain 6,957 FP32 and 7,506 FP16 hierarchy-tagged nodes.

not_yet_tested_on: artifacts with nested graph owners or local functions

gotchas: In-memory trace coverage is not persistence evidence; save/reload the final artifact and count serialized winml.hierarchy.* properties.
findings.mechanism_notes: Focused save/reload and destructive-pipeline tests plus final tester structure manifests confirm persistence.
